title: Mexico on the Verge of Leaving the Hunger Map
author: Laura Poy Solano
content:
_This article by[Laura Poy
Solano](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Laura%20Poy%20Solano) originally
appeared in the [October 17, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/2026/10/17/politica/008n1pol), Mexico's
premier left wing daily newspaper._

In a global context with multiple challenges for food production, Mexico "is
doing well," said Lina Pohl Alfaro, representative of the **United Nations
Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)** in our country.

On the occasion of World Food Day, which was celebrated yesterday, she
stressed that while in many countries the interests of large corporations are
placed above the common good, here "the exact opposite is being done: **more
than 8 million people left poverty** , that is, they left hunger. And Mexico
is about to leave the hunger map that the FAO builds, it is very close," she
said.

> Let's set aside pettiness and unite. We have to leave aside any ideology, we
> are doing well.
>
> Lina Pohl Alfaro, FAO representative in Mexico

![A farmer tends a nopal field](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/10/mexico-leaving-hunger-map-fao-02-nopal.jpg)The country
"is doing well" in food production, said Lina Pohl Alfaro, the organization's
representative in our country. Photo: Marco Peláez

For her part, the Secretary of Agriculture and Rural Development (Sader),
Columba López, announced support actions for the **19 communities** in the
municipalities of Chilapa de Álvarez and Olinalá, in the Montaña Alta region
of Guerrero, where farmers suffered displacement.

Among the actions that, she said, the federal government will carry out is the
delivery of 250 maize seeds, with which the production of grains for
distribution and planting in the area will begin. In addition, she said, they
will be guaranteed the delivery of **maize and beans for 19 months** , so that
"they have food, while agricultural production gets back on its feet."

At that event, which brought together farmers from the Montaña Alta of
Guerrero who participate in the Sembrando Vida and Jóvenes Construyendo el
Futuro programs, Lina Pohl recalled that in the world **more than 700 million
people** suffer from hunger. "And it is not a problem of food production, but
of how, how much, what and who are included in production," since of the total
cost that consumers pay for their food, **only 25 percent** reaches the hands
of those who sowed, tended and cultivated it.

Accompanied by Dr. Daniel Aceves, director general of Public Health of the
Secretariat of Health, and by César Abarca García, director general of
Development and Innovation of Sader, who stressed that to strengthen the
transformation actions in the Mexican countryside, it is not only necessary to
recognize and reinforce the leadership of women farmers and producers, but
also access to machinery that "they can use and that is adapted to work on
smaller agricultural plots."

The specialists agreed that the world faces various food challenges, from
climate change to the effects of the wars spreading across various regions of
the planet and the constant pressure of large corporations that seek to impose
their interests, even at the cost of driving up food prices.
